name: Django settings for conversationalBI project.  Generated by 'django-admin startp
summary: Central Django configuration module that bootstraps the conversationalBI project by defining core runtime settings, loading environment variables, and establishing project-wide parameters.
purpose: Provides a single source of truth for all Django runtime configuration, enabling environment-specific deployments (local, staging, production) while keeping sensitive credentials and host-specific values out of version control through the use of django-environ and environment variables.
responsibilities: Define core Django project settings such as DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, ALLOWED_HOSTS, and LANGUAGE_CODE
Load and parse environment variables and optional .env files via django-environ
Configure database connections, caching backends, and static/media file paths
Register INSTALLED_APPS and define MIDDLEWARE pipelines
Establish project root and base directory paths using pathlib.Path
Set localization, timezone, logging, and security defaults
Separate sensitive credentials from version-controlled source code
inputs: Django framework defaults and runtime expectations
outputs: Django settings namespace (module-level configuration constants consumed by django.conf)
Configured Path objects for project, application, and asset directories
Bootstrapped runtime environment for the conversationalBI application stack
architecture_notes: Implements Django's mandatory centralized configuration pattern, acting as the implicit contract between the framework and the application runtime. Uses django-environ to follow 12-factor app principles, externalizing configuration and secrets into the environment. The adoption of pathlib.Path over os.path indicates a modern Python approach. Its location at backend/config/settings.py suggests a custom, nested project layout—common in monorepos or containerized architectures—that isolates server-side code from repository root artifacts. All settings are module-level constants, which Django imports lazily, making this module a hot path for every management command, WSGI/ASGI worker, and Celery process.
improvements: Refactor into a settings package (base.py, local.py, production.py, test.py) to prevent accidental production misconfiguration and reduce merge conflicts
Add strict startup validation for required environment variables (e.g., DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY) with descriptive error messages to fail fast on misconfigured deployments
Introduce type hints or Pydantic/django-configurations models for complex nested settings like DATABASES, LOGGING, and AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS
Move non-sensitive defaults and third-party app configurations into dedicated mixin modules to improve readability
Document conversationalBI-specific custom settings with inline docstrings to clarify coupling between configuration and business logic
Consider using dynaconf or django-configurations for inheritance, type safety, and cleaner environment-specific overrides
